slides.1.title: Sercial and Verdelho: Dry Madeira
slides.1.html:
🍋 Sercial (very dry)

  • Planted in the highest-altitude (700–900m) vineyards on Madeira, the coolest zone on the island
  • Late ripening; still very high in acidity at harvest, with low residual sugar
  • Style: very dry / dry (about ≤49–59 g/L), highest acidity, crisp and mineral, with almond・brine・iodine・smoke aromas
  • Best served: chilled (8–10°C) as an aperitif, with olives・nuts・rich seafood soups
  • Ageing potential: Sercial of 10–50 years can show astonishing complexity

🌿 Verdelho (medium dry)

  • Planted at medium altitude (400–700m), ripening slightly more than Sercial
  • Style: Meio Seco, medium dry (about 54–78 g/L), slightly sweet with high acidity and distinctive smoky・vanilla・golden apple aromas
  • Best served: lightly chilled (10–12°C), with poached seafood and vegetable soups
  • Historically the Madeira style most loved by the British market
slides.2.title: Bual and Malvasia: Sweet Madeira
slides.2.html:
🟤 Bual (= Boal) (medium sweet)

  • Planted at low to medium altitude (200–400m), a warmer zone, ripening earlier
  • Style: Meio Doce, medium sweet (about 78–100 g/L), deep golden brown, with complex fig・toffee・caramel・cocoa flavours
  • Acidity is still sufficient to support the sweetness, so it never seems heavy
  • Best served: at room temperature (16–18°C), with blue cheese・walnut desserts・chocolate

🍯 Malvasia (= Malmsey) (very sweet)

  • Planted in the lowest-altitude (0–200m) coastal zone, the warmest, with the highest sugar levels
  • Style: Doce, sweet (about ≥100 g/L), deep amber, with honey・apricot・tropical fruit・orange marmalade
  • Although very sweet, Madeira's high acidity stops it cloying, leaving it silky and luscious
  • Best served: slightly warm (16°C), as an after-dinner sweet wine, with custard tarts・rich pastries・foie gras
  • The most popular Madeira style on the market, and the first choice for beginners

📋 Madeira Without a Grape Variety on the Label

  • Most inexpensive Madeira does not state a variety and is a blend based on Tinta Negra Mole (the most widely planted variety on the island)
  • Sweetness may be stated: Seco (very dry)・Medium Dry・Medium Rich・Rich (very sweet)

slides.4.question: Of the four Madeira varieties, which is planted at the highest altitude (700–900m) and has the highest acidity and lowest sweetness?
slides.4.explanation: Sercial is planted in Madeira's highest-altitude vineyards (700–900m), making it the coolest-grown and latest-ripening variety. It therefore has the highest acidity and lowest sweetness, giving a very dry style with mineral, briny and almond aromas, and is the Madeira style best suited as an aperitif.
slides.5.question: Malvasia (Malmsey) is the sweetest of the four Madeira varieties, so why does it not taste cloying?
slides.5.options.0: Because its alcohol is low (11%), making it fresher
slides.5.options.1: Because Madeira's maderisation process reduces the sugar
slides.5.options.2: Because Madeira's naturally high acidity (even in the sweetest styles) balances the sweetness so that it does not cloy
slides.5.options.3: Because Malvasia grapes themselves contain bitter compounds
slides.5.explanation: Madeira is known for its extremely high natural acidity. Even the sweetest Malvasia (about ≥100 g/L, Doce) retains plenty of acidity through the maderisation process, giving the sweetness a solid acid backbone, so it is silky and luscious rather than cloying. This is the biggest difference between sweet Madeira and other sweet wines.
